fixes.explanation: Peter says the opposite, friend. He calls himself "…a witness of Christ’s sufferings…" (1 Peter 5:1). That matters, because he's writing to people who are in the middle of a hard season. He also says he's a partaker of the glory to be revealed, so his words come from someone who saw it.

Close, because Paul uses a building picture when he says, "…you are God’s field, God’s building." (1 Corinthians 3:9). But here Peter says, "Be shepherds of God’s flock that is among you…" (1 Peter 5:2). A flock needs watching over, not a hammer. The elders are looking after people, and the flock belongs to God.

That's it, friend. Peter says, "…not lording it over those entrusted to you, but being examples to the flock." (1 Peter 5:3). The elders lead by showing the way, not by bossing people around. An example is something the flock can see.

Nope, friend. Peter says the adversary prowls around like a roaring lion, "…seeking someone to devour." (1 Peter 5:8). He's hunting, not looking for a place to hide. That's why Peter says to be sober-minded and alert.

Yes, friend. Peter says to stand firm "…in the knowledge that your brothers throughout the world are undergoing the same kinds of suffering." (1 Peter 5:9). That's worth knowing when a trial feels lonely. Peter's readers aren't the only ones in it, because their brothers throughout the world are in it too.

Timothy is a name you may know, friend. Paul opens 1 Thessalonians with "Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy…" (1 Thessalonians 1:1). But Peter writes, "Through Silvanus, whom I regard as a faithful brother, I have written to you briefly…" (1 Peter 5:12). Silvanus is the name here.
